  "title": "SVN process is broken",
  "body": "Current SVN process is broken. It needs to re-visit the existing procedures and investigate what changes it needs to apply to work with current code-base. ",
  "author": "Participant 1",
  "created_at": "2018-06-14T08:41:31Z",
  "updated_at": "2018-09-11T23:44:34Z",
  "state": "closed",
  "closed_at": null,
  "issue_fetched_at": "2026-11-05T06:24:03.898405+00:00",

    "2026-11-05T06:24:03.898405+00:00"
  ],
  "expected_comment_count": 18,
  "retrieved_comment_count": 15,
  "comments_complete": false,
  "comments": [
    {
      "id": 408912309,
      "url": "https://github.com/Moonshine-IDE/Moonshine-IDE/issues/307#issuecomment-408912309",
      "created_at": "2018-07-30T15:50:13Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-30T16:05:20Z",
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "I didn't liked the existing structure to SVN in Moonshine, but I don't want to waste effort to recreating the wheel completely. Instead, I chose to keep in the way it had been, fixed problems and modified some areas to use newer checkout and selection/commit windows that used in Git, with updated logic.\r\n\r\nFollowing things has only tested on Windows so far:\r\n\r\n- SVN options other than 'Checkout' now part of the top menu only, i.e. Commit, Update etc. - like Git menu options - they enables/disables upon testing the current project if SVN repository:\r\n`svn ls <projectFolder>`\r\n- Previous context-menu options for SVN to sidebar now removed\r\n- SVN Checkout now uses existing Git checkout window with conditional logic - checkout procedure fixed - I'm not sure about more fine-tuned validation (like we have in Git checkout) on this case, though\r\n- SVN Commit now uses existing Git selection/commit window. Requisite logic updated in SVN files to work with the popup codes - tested against file deletion, addition (unversioned) and modification\r\n\r\nI have tested with TortoiseSVN on Windows (make sure you have command-line support installed in the installation steps).\r\n\r\n_Note:_ SVN repository test command takes some seconds to complete - so some time this may take some seconds to enable the menus under Subversion.\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 409448775,
      "url": "https://github.com/Moonshine-IDE/Moonshine-IDE/issues/307#issuecomment-409448775",
      "created_at": "2018-08-01T04:52:52Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-08-02T10:17:17Z",
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "### Todo:\r\n\r\n- [x] Append possible folder name at the end of the target path in Checkout dialog\r\n- [ ] Finalizing macOS run\r\n\r\n### Bugs:\r\n\r\n- [ ] Setting binary on macOS throws error (`/usr/bin/svn`)"
    },
    {
      "id": 409547510,
      "url": "https://github.com/Moonshine-IDE/Moonshine-IDE/issues/307#issuecomment-409547510",
      "created_at": "2018-08-01T11:46:26Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-08-01T12:55:25Z",
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "Debugging more on `/usr/bin/svn` file selection through Objc-c file dialog in sandbox, it returns following error:\r\n\r\n```\r\n\"Error Domain=NSCocoaErrorDomain Code=256 \"Could not open() the item\"\r\nUserInfo={NSURL=file:///usr/bin/svn, NSDebugDescription=Could not open() the item}\"\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe closest reason found at https://stackoverflow.com/questions/49206548/error-domain-nscocoaerrordomain-code-256 which match the using file format (`/usr/bin/svn` vs `file:///usr/bin/svn`); However, looking into the Obj-C codes I'm not at this moment sure where the said type-casting is happening. I need to look more into this.\r\n\r\nI also have added an alert to Moonshine when such error return by the extension.\r\n\r\nIt seems like local Obj-C/extension-preparation setup messed up. I need to fix these setup again. "
    },
    {
      "id": 409849676,
      "url": "https://github.com/Moonshine-IDE/Moonshine-IDE/issues/307#issuecomment-409849676",
      "created_at": "2018-08-02T08:32:25Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-08-02T08:32:43Z",
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "Reading different discussion from here and there, the one most close scenario that found can cause `Error Domain=NSCocoaErrorDomain Code=256 Could not open() the item` error is when try to access a file with not properly construct as NSURL/URL for the file system purpose, i.e.\r\n\r\n`URL(string: dataURLString);`\r\n\r\ninstead of \r\n\r\n`URL(fileURLWithPath: dataURLString)`\r\n\r\nBut every items returned by `NSOpenPanel` are fully-compliant `NSURL` objects. We are not preparing or constructing any NSURL/URL manually so we could have a chance of creating/using problematic `NSURL` pointer. \r\n\r\nI find out that the error throws when the URL/NSURL tries to add with bookmark scope in the Obj-c code. I even created new `NSURL` object constructing with suggested API and tried to add to bookmark scope, but `/usr/bin/svn` continued to throw same error. \r\n\r\nI tried a little hacky way. I know this may not be a right way of doing this, but we can take this as ethical hacking for the purpose. When `/usr/bin/svn` returns the file access error, I tried to auto-bookmark the parent directory of it `/usr/bin`. That did go well and didn't thrown any error. I have checked in Access Manager list (as returns by the extension) added with `/usr/bin` path.\r\n\r\nWhen I tried to checkout a SVN path to my system, the execution thrown following error on console:\r\n`: xcrun: error: cannot be used within an App Sandbox.`\r\n\r\nI can remember we had such `xcrun` error situation in past, but I can't able to remember now where and when; or what was the resolution.\r\n\r\nFor the time being, I'm restoring the extension to all old codes. "
    },
    {
      "id": 409879636,
      "url": "https://github.com/Moonshine-IDE/Moonshine-IDE/issues/307#issuecomment-409879636",
      "created_at": "2018-08-02T10:20:28Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "Target folder path now append with possible folder name value; assuming by basic regexp check as was in Git:\r\n\r\n`(svn|http|https|file)://(domainName)/(lastComponentPath)`\r\n\r\nTarget folder path always constructs now with the `lastComponentPath`. i.e. \r\n\r\n```\r\nURL: https://svn-mySite.com/subFolder/trunk/Moonshine\r\nPath: C:/Users/MyName/Desktop/Moonshine\r\n```"
    },
    {
      "id": 410230375,
      "url": "https://github.com/Moonshine-IDE/Moonshine-IDE/issues/307#issuecomment-410230375",
      "created_at": "2018-08-03T11:49:57Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-08-03T11:50:16Z",
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "https://forums.developer.apple.com/message/89866#89866\r\n\r\n> : svn: E170013: Unable to connect to a repository at URL 'https://svn-mysite.com/svn/trunk/AIRAppNapTest'\r\n> : svn: E230001: Server SSL certificate verification failed: issuer is not trusted"
    },
    {
      "id": 411413295,
      "url": "https://github.com/Moonshine-IDE/Moonshine-IDE/issues/307#issuecomment-411413295",
      "created_at": "2018-08-08T13:53:01Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "`Subversion` menu options now enables upon existence checking of `./svn/wc.db` file to the project root.\r\n\r\nIn macOS, if an auth already present against certain SVN URL to keychain, Moonshine will continue using that information while `Update` and `Commit` from/to the URL.\r\n\r\nHowever, if no auth present and update/commit returned by authentication failure message, Moonshine now open the same authentication window that used to Git auth. Upon providing necessary information, Moonshine will re-try to complete previously failed process. \r\n\r\nOnce a _successful_ auth stored to keychain, user will not require to provide auth information again against certain SVN URL.\r\n\r\nThe above changes can be done by deleting named SVN password entry from the keychain in macOS. \r\n\r\n[_NOTE_: All tests done to macOS so far, Windows' tests pending. The way codes have done to SVN process is a mess and worst to an height - I only tried to fix the parts which requires to support above process, instead of re-inventing the full-workflow.]"
    },
    {
      "id": 411463463,
      "url": "https://github.com/Moonshine-IDE/Moonshine-IDE/issues/307#issuecomment-411463463",
      "created_at": "2018-08-08T16:13:24Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "I got a certificate validation prompt on my checkout attempts:\r\n\r\n    : Error validating server certificate for 'https://<censored>:443':\r\n    :  - The certificate is not issued by a trusted authority. Use the\r\n    :    fingerprint to validate the certificate manually!\r\n    : Certificate information:\r\n    :  - Hostname: <censored>\r\n    :  - Valid: from Mon, 19 Mar 2018 00:00:00 GMT until Tue, 11 Jun 2019 23:59:59 GMT\r\n    :  - Issuer: COMODO CA Limited, Salford, Greater Manchester, GB\r\n    :  - Fingerprint: <censored>\r\n    : (R)eject, accept (t)emporarily or accept (p)ermanently? \r\n\r\nI don't see an option to add the additional certificate arguments.\r\n\r\n\r\nI manually checked out a project, but my authentication were rejected when I did an Update or Commit:\r\n\r\n    : svn: E170001: \r\n    : Unable to connect to a repository at URL 'https://<censored>/svn/sh-flex/branches/TestMoonshineSubversionJoel'\r\n    : svn: E170001: OPTIONS of 'https://<censored>/svn/sh-flex/branches/TestMoonshineSubversionJoel': authorization failed: Could not authenticate to server: rejected Basic challenge (https://<censored>)\r\n\r\nI didn't get an authentication popup in my tests.\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 411486541,
      "url": "https://github.com/Moonshine-IDE/Moonshine-IDE/issues/307#issuecomment-411486541",
      "created_at": "2018-08-08T17:26:00Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "The prompt for authentication triggers based on certain message type, i.e. authentication failed. In this case it's rejection against some challenge - probably the challenge were in form of Reject, Accept and Accept Permanently. \r\n\r\nI noticed that checkout command was missing the extra arguments like `--non-interactive` etc. when other commands were added with them. You can give a try with the newer build, @JoelProminic , although since Update and Commit already has those extra arguments, I'm not sure why they're not trusting certificate and turning to challenge failure. (Maybe that is because the Accept|Reject prompt didn't affect at first place (?))\r\n\r\nI'm not sure how to get this Accept|Reject error - maybe removing the Comodo certificate completely from Keychain would avail that - I'm not sure. "
    },
    {
      "id": 411655524,
      "url": "https://github.com/Moonshine-IDE/Moonshine-IDE/issues/307#issuecomment-411655524",
      "created_at": "2018-08-09T06:50:05Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "To able to get the error report containing `Accept | Reject | Accept Permanently`, I tried following things:\r\n\r\n1. I had following items in my system's keychain (ignore the date values - screenshot taken after completing all these steps)\r\n![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/24370870/43882567-b88c5cce-9bcd-11e8-89f6-b706cced7a5a.png)\r\n2. I only able to delete the last item from the list - other two items simply not deletes - while the first item thrown - `UNIX[Operation not permitted]`\r\n3. I tried to checkout with Moonshine but I didn't reported by the `Accept | Reject` error with current build\r\n4. I also changed the trust mode of the existing certificates to 'Never Trust' - but that didn't make any difference either \r\n\r\nI'm not sure at this moment how to get into the environment when the said type of error fires, so I can debug further. "
    },
    {
      "id": 419209246,
      "url": "https://github.com/Moonshine-IDE/Moonshine-IDE/issues/307#issuecomment-419209246",
      "created_at": "2018-09-06T19:12:51Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "I have retested the SVN certificate issue, and it no longer triggers for me on either OS X Yosemite or macOS High Sierra.   \r\n\r\n@rat-moonshine reported that Moonshine is currently using --trust-server-cert.  This setting should not be enabled by default, so please allow this to be enabled in a checkbox (similar to how authentication is working for the Checkout prompt).  \r\n\r\nThis selection can be persisted in the application or project settings.  Putting it in the project settings will allow the setting to be controlled for individual projects, so that the certificate will be  consistently ignored for a specific project.  Saving it at the application level will be convenient if all of the projects are from the same repository, but it is problematic if the user uses multiple SVN servers with different certificates.  I think using the Project settings is probably better, but I am open to discussion on this.\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 419432040,
      "url": "https://github.com/Moonshine-IDE/Moonshine-IDE/issues/307#issuecomment-419432040",
      "created_at": "2018-09-07T13:01:32Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-09-07T13:02:43Z",
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "New option added to project's Settings: `Subversion > Trust server certificate` (default _false_?)\r\n\r\nThe above option is suppose to available if user has subversion configured (to Moonshine) and the project is a subversion project. I yet to connect the property to related SVN commands in Moonshine."
    },
    {
      "id": 419864368,
      "url": "https://github.com/Moonshine-IDE/Moonshine-IDE/issues/307#issuecomment-419864368",
      "created_at": "2018-09-10T10:24:04Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "- Project level trust server certificate option now incorporated with the SVN command execution\r\n- Another level of trust server certificate option added to the Moonshine Settings as `SVN > Checkout` task do not depends on any project"
    },
    {
      "id": 420153596,
      "url": "https://github.com/Moonshine-IDE/Moonshine-IDE/issues/307#issuecomment-420153596",
      "created_at": "2018-09-11T05:42:59Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "- Trust certificate option now relocated to the Checkout window from Moonshine Settings\r\n- Checkout window now waits until the first response back from Git - to determine if its an error or results - based on that the window either report to check error details on console (as user may have console minimized or shrink to minimal height) and remain the inputs intact, or, close the window"
    },
    {
      "id": 420463213,
      "url": "https://github.com/Moonshine-IDE/Moonshine-IDE/issues/307#issuecomment-420463213",
      "created_at": "2018-09-11T23:44:34Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "I updated this in CHANGELOG.md.   \r\n\r\nHave you updated Windows with the \"Trust certificate\" option?   I thought of this at the end of the day and did not have a chance to test."
    }
  ],
